clue.text: Authority for traveller to proceed to the left?

parts.note: to pass is to go on or proceed
port is the left-hand side of a ship

explanation.surface: A question about whether a traveller has permission to set off leftwards.
explanation.definitionFit: The document is the official permission a person carries to cross borders.

clue.text: Wood not big enough to be a general favourite

indicators.note: falling short in size means the word for a favourite is one letter too short

parts.note: something widely liked is popular

explanation.surface: Some timber fails to win wide approval.
explanation.walkthrough: 'not big enough' drops U from POPULAR.
explanation.definitionFit: A tall fast-growing tree yields a soft pale timber.

clue.text: Used to catch fish, or alligator perhaps, in a vessel

indicators.note: one piece is placed inside the other

parts.note: SS is a steamship
the alligator pear is the avocado, a kind of pear

explanation.surface: Hunting fish, or perhaps an alligator, from a boat.
explanation.walkthrough: 'alligator' is not the reptile: an alligator pear is an avocado, so it is a type of PEAR.
explanation.definitionFit: Pointed thrusting weapons are used by fishers to impale their catch.

clue.text: No oil required, presumably, for these waters

definitions.text: No oil required, presumably, for these waters

parts.words: No oil required, presumably, for these waters
parts.note: pouring oil on troubled waters calms them; an ocean named for being peaceful should need none

explanation.definitionFit: The ocean was named for its calm, so its waters are already tranquil.

clue.text: Take in sails as rocks appear

definitions.meaning: to shorten sail by rolling or folding part of it
a ridge of rocks near the surface of the sea

explanation.definitionFit: The word means both shortening sail and an underwater ridge.

clue.text: Approved some time back, we hear

indicators.note: says the word meant is one heard spoken, so its sound gives the letters

parts.note: past means gone by, some time ago

explanation.surface: Someone recalls hearing that a measure got the nod a while ago.
explanation.definitionFit: A motion that is voted through has been approved by the house.

clue.text: Plant article on companion going to America

parts.note: an is the indefinite article
CH stands for Companion of Honour
USA is America

explanation.surface: A piece about a friend travelling to the States.
explanation.walkthrough: CH is the British honour Companion of Honour.
explanation.definitionFit: Alkanet, a bristly blue-flowered herb of the borage family, is this plant.

clue.text: Deploying asdic around Manx port at irregular intervals

indicators.note: one set of letters goes around the other
deploying spreads out and arranges the letters of asdic afresh
a Manx cat has no tail, so the word port loses its final letter

explanation.surface: A ship uses sonar around an Isle of Man harbour every now and then.
explanation.walkthrough: ASDIC was an early sonar, and the Manx cat has no tail, which is why 'Manx' docks the last letter of the harbour word.
explanation.definitionFit: Something occasional and scattered happens only now and then.

clue.text: Rogue indulged in trickery

indicators.note: rogue as an adjective means wild and errant, so the letters of indulged run astray

explanation.surface: A scoundrel gave in to cheating.
explanation.walkthrough: 'in' is a link; the definition is the noun sense of the -ING form, the act of misleading.
explanation.definitionFit: Misleading people, as an activity, is deception.

clue.text: Caper around with the girl, he advocates

indicators.note: the letters of caper are turned around into a new order

parts.note: her is the pronoun for a girl

explanation.surface: A man who frolics with a girl turns out to be a campaigner.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Caper' looks like the subject doing the frolicking, but it is only letters to rearrange.
explanation.definitionFit: A minister in the pulpit is someone who urges and champions a cause or faith.

clue.text: Train some porpoises

definitions.meaning: to educate or drill someone, as a verb
the collective noun for a group of porpoises or fish

explanation.definitionFit: The word means both to teach and a shoal of sea creatures swimming together.

clue.text: Boats either side of the river catching a great number of them?

definitions.text: Boats either side of the river catching a great number of them?

indicators.note: catching means taking something inside, so a letter goes within
the boats word lies on both sides of the river letter

parts.note: ships are boats
R is the abbreviation for river
M is a thousand in Roman numerals

explanation.surface: Fishing boats on a river haul in vast numbers of small crustaceans.
explanation.walkthrough: 'either side of' puts SHIPS round R (SHRIPS); 'catching' then puts M inside.
explanation.definitionFit: Small edible crustaceans are netted in large quantities by trawlers.

clue.text: Commercial break without purpose

parts.note: an ad is a commercial
a rift is a break or split

explanation.surface: An advertisement interval seems to go on aimlessly.
explanation.definitionFit: Something drifting with no direction or aim is said to be floating loose.

clue.text: Hand-outs distributed in large number

indicators.note: the letters of hand-outs are dealt out and spread into a new order

explanation.surface: A great many free gifts are given away.
explanation.definitionFit: A figure of one followed by three zeros is a sizeable number.

clue.text: In large characters, decorate the rim

indicators.note: the characters, meaning letters, of in large are reshuffled

explanation.surface: Using big letters to ornament the border.
explanation.walkthrough: 'characters' means the letters of IN LARGE, rearranged.
explanation.definitionFit: In heraldry and coin-making, to indent an edge with curved notches is to ornament it.

clue.text: Such people analyse discordant noise of birds

parts.note: to scan is to examine closely
din is a loud clashing noise
avian means relating to birds

explanation.surface: Some nationality is said to study the racket made by birds.
explanation.walkthrough: The definition leans on the clue as a whole: people of a certain kind, from Norway, Sweden or Denmark.
explanation.definitionFit: Natives of the northern European countries of Norway, Sweden and Denmark are this sort of people.

clue.text: Plant in a metal container in this way

parts.note: a can is a tin
thus means in this manner

explanation.surface: A plant is grown in a tin, like so.
explanation.definitionFit: Bear's breech, whose leaves inspired classical column carvings, is this plant.

clue.text: The way to encourage fish production

parts.note: ST is short for street, a way
to urge on is to encourage

explanation.surface: How to boost the output of a fishery.
explanation.walkthrough: 'production' is a link here, part of the surface about a fishery.
explanation.definitionFit: A large bony-plated fish whose roe is caviar.

clue.text: His Croat pact unfortunately proves disastrous

indicators.note: an unlucky outcome signals the letters of his Croat pact being thrown into disorder

explanation.surface: A treaty signed by a Croatian turns out badly.
explanation.definitionFit: A ruinous outcome is a catastrophe, so something ruinous is calamitous.

clue.text: Lifting instruments, to deliver a shanty aboard ship

indicators.note: aboard means on a vessel, so a piece goes inside the ship letters

parts.note: SS is a steamship
a shanty is a hovel, a poor hut

explanation.surface: Sailors sing a sea song while hauling on deck.
explanation.walkthrough: 'shanty' is a shack here, not a sea song.
explanation.definitionFit: Spades with broad scoops are tools for raising and moving earth or coal.

clue.text: Evening job

parts.note: evening read as making even or flat, a household chore with a hot appliance

explanation.definitionFit: Pressing clothes smooth is the task of making them flat.

clue.text: Where small party turned up with a large snake?

indicators.note: in a down clue, turned up means the word is read from bottom to top

parts.note: Lab is the short form of Labour, a party
a boa is a large constricting snake

explanation.surface: A question about where a little group came across a big serpent.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Where' defines a place: Balboa is the port at the Pacific end of the Panama Canal.
explanation.definitionFit: A port city in Panama is a location, answering the question of place.

clue.text: Casts 'off rags when, plunging in river

indicators.note: plunging in means diving into, so one piece enters the other

parts.note: to shed is to cast off

explanation.surface: Someone throws off their ragged clothes before diving into a river.
explanation.walkthrough: 'plunging in' puts R inside SHEDS; 'when' is a link.
explanation.definitionFit: Tattered scraps of cloth are torn strips.

clue.text: Navy scouring Arctic circle to get a drug

indicators.note: scouring suggests ranging over and stirring up the letters of Arctic and the circle

parts.note: O is a circle by its shape

explanation.surface: A naval vessel searches the polar region for illicit substances.
explanation.walkthrough: 'scouring' looks like searching, but here it signals stirring the letters of Arctic and the circle together.
explanation.definitionFit: An opiate or other sleep-inducing substance is this kind of drug.

clue.text: Chemical needed, to plant out a tree

parts.note: to pot a seedling is to plant it in a container
the ash is a tree

explanation.surface: A gardener needs a fertiliser to set out a sapling.
explanation.walkthrough: 'a' joins the pieces; 'needed' is a link.
explanation.definitionFit: Potassium carbonate, used in fertilisers, is a common alkaline compound.

clue.text: Open with a French act

parts.note: un is French for a
to do is to act

explanation.surface: Starting with a French performance.
explanation.definitionFit: To unfasten a knot or button is to unfasten or loosen it.

clue.text: Noted male newsmen

parts.note: he is the male pronoun
two editors, each an ed, are the newsmen

explanation.surface: Some men of the press were well known.
explanation.walkthrough: The plural 'newsmen' gives two EDs, each ED being an editor.
explanation.definitionFit: To have noted a warning is to have paid attention to it.

clue.text: Privileged, getting permit to entertain six

indicators.note: to entertain a guest is to hold them within, so one piece goes inside the other

parts.note: to enable is to permit
VI is six in Roman numerals

explanation.surface: Someone lucky is allowed to host a group of six.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Privileged' here means fortunately placed, a position others would want.
explanation.definitionFit: A fortunate, favoured position is one others would covet.

clue.text: Salvation Army home for those who were once termed healthiest

parts.note: a nest is a home

explanation.surface: A charity hostel for those once called the fittest.
explanation.walkthrough: 'for those who were once termed' signals an old sense: from Latin sanus, sane once meant sound in body as well as mind.
explanation.definitionFit: Being of sound mind once also meant being in good bodily condition, so most sound means fittest.

clue.text: Pines bordering the road from one end to the other

definitions.text: from one end to the other

indicators.note: one word lies at the edges of the other, enclosing it

parts.note: to pine is to long
a way is a road

explanation.surface: Pine trees line a road along its length.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Pines' reads as trees lining the road, but it is a verb meaning yearns.
explanation.definitionFit: Lengthwise means running along the full length of something.
